A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAPKV research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LongBench and AIME25 evaluations, capacity–performance correlations, temperature ablations, and runtime measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds approximation ablations, quantization experiments, and LongBench v2 evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same capacity matrix, value-vector proxy, mean-query weighting, leverage scores, and selection procedure. Exact-output and covariance alternatives are evaluated as ablations without changing default CAPKV.

E1.justification: Section 4.6 adds LongBench v2 evaluation on 118 samples with 32K–128K contexts, including inputs requiring extension beyond the model's native window. This substantially extends benchmark and context-length coverage; the original LongBench, AIME25, and appendix evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding experiments is unchanged. The added quantization and LongBench v2 comparisons use EA, KeyDiff, KNorm, and SnapKV, already compared with Qwen3-8B in Table 1. Sink remains in its original comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds distinct evaluation protocols using 4-bit HQQ on retained caches and YaRN context extrapolation. It also adds controlled approximation comparisons on five LongBench subsets at compression ratios 0.5 and 0.75. These supplement unchanged original protocols rather than establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Expanded Section 4.4 directly tests two previously untested approximations: value vectors versus projected output directions, and mean-query versus diagonal-covariance gating. Section 4.5 adds robustness testing under quantization. The original temperature ablation is retained as Table 3.

E5.justification: Spearman correlations and p-value reporting are unchanged, as is Appendix C.1's five timed runs after one warm-up. The added experiments introduce no seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Tables 2, 4, and 5 substantially expand reported findings. At compression 0.75, Table 2 reports averages of 52.64 for default CAPKV, 52.87 for exact output directions, and 49.22 for covariance gating. Table 5 reports CAPKV scores of 43.7, 47.9, and 44.8: it leads at compression 0.75 and 0.9 but trails SnapKV's 46.2 at 0.5. Original results, including appendix tables, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds an asymptotic-cost comparison between the default proxy, O(Nd²+d³), and exact output directions, O(N(dh)²+(dh)³). The core assumptions, theorem, lemma, and mathematical analyses in appendices A–B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a unified information-capacity interpretation, leverage-based CAPKV, and improved fidelity–memory trade-offs. New experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds result-based arguments for the efficiency of the value proxy, attributes covariance gating's degradation to noisy finite-history estimation, and discusses compatibility with quantization and extended contexts. Existing surrogate-model limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code repository hyperlink. New experiment descriptions specify 4-bit HQQ and YaRN usage; existing hardware, global temperature, and runtime details in Appendix C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for HQQ, LongBench v2, and YaRN, and removes the KeepKV citation and reference. The broader positioning relative to attention-based and structural eviction methods is retained.

P1.justification: V2 lightly edits the introduction, expands Section 4.4, adds Sections 4.5–4.6 and acknowledgments, and updates affiliation and publication text. The main narrative and appendix structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three compact experimental tables, relocates the retained temperature table, and redraws the polyhedral illustrations in Figure 2. Other figures and existing table structures are largely preserved, with local resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new design ablations directly strengthen support for CAPKV's approximations, while extended-context evaluation and the code link improve empirical scope and reproducibility information. However, the quantization evidence has unresolved reporting problems: Table 4's CAPKV average at compression 0.5 is 55.47, whereas its six displayed scores average 57.31, and comparator scores repeat Table 1 despite the newly stated setting. These weaknesses limit the gains, but the independently useful ablations and extended-context results support a modest net improvement.
